target: La personne dont tu as besoin viendra demain.
english: The person you need will come tomorrow.
tip: Avoir besoin de → dont: "la personne dont tu as besoin."

target: Voici le restaurant qui fait les meilleures pizzas.
english: Here's the restaurant that makes the best pizzas.
tip: "Qui" is used for subjects: le restaurant fait → le restaurant qui fait.

target: Si j'avais le temps, je voyagerais plus souvent.
english: If I had time, I would travel more often.
tip: Never put a conditional after si. The 'would' verb sits in the other clause: si j'avais (had), je voyagerais (would travel).

target: Il faudrait que tu prennes rendez-vous chez le dentiste.
english: You should make an appointment at the dentist.
tip: 'Il faudrait que' + subjunctive – conditional of 'falloir' for polite necessity: 'you should...'

target: Ça me plairait de vivre dans un pays chaud.
english: I would enjoy living in a warm country.
tip: Plaire flips the subject: ça me plairait is literally 'it would please me', not 'I would like it'. The thing you enjoy does the pleasing.

target: Tu n'auras qu'à me passer un coup de fil.
english: You'll just have to give me a call.
tip: N'avoir qu'à means 'to only have to', i.e. just: tu n'auras qu'à me passer un coup de fil = you'll just have to give me a call.

target: La robe que tu portes te va très bien.
english: The dress you're wearing looks great on you.
tip: Clothes 'go' on you in French: te va très bien means 'suits you', from aller (to go). Ça te va = it looks good on you.

target: La réunion aura lieu dans la salle de conférence.
english: The meeting will take place in the conference room.
tip: An event doesn't 'happen', it 'has place': avoir lieu = to take place. La réunion aura lieu = the meeting will take place.

target: J'adorerais visiter le Japon un jour.
english: I would love to visit Japan someday.
tip: Countries carry an article in French: le Japon, not just 'Japan'. You visit le Japon, la France, les États-Unis.

target: Le spectacle commencera à vingt heures.
english: The show will start at 8 PM.
tip: France runs on the 24-hour clock: vingt heures is 8 PM, not 20 in the morning. Subtract 12 to get the evening time.

target: Le livre que j'ai lu est passionnant.
english: The book I read is fascinating.
tip: 'que' recycles the object into a connector: 'j'ai lu le livre' becomes 'le livre que j'ai lu' = the book (that) I read.

target: Si j'avais ton talent, je deviendrais artiste.
english: If I had your talent, I would become an artist.
tip: Drop the article before a profession: je deviendrais artiste, not 'un artiste'. French names the job bare – il est médecin.

target: Bien qu'il eût raison, personne ne le croyait.
english: Although he was right, no one believed him.
tip: Imperfect subjunctive of avoir: eût. Literary equivalent of 'bien qu'il ait raison'.

target: Dès qu'il fera beau, nous irons à la plage.
english: As soon as the weather is nice, we'll go to the beach.
tip: After "dès que" and "quand," French uses the futur simple, unlike English.

target: Ils travailleront ensemble l'année prochaine.
english: They will work together next year.
tip: French has two futures: futur simple ('je travaillerai' – more formal/distant) and futur proche ('je vais travailler' – imminent/certain).

target: Ils se marieront l'été prochain.
english: They will get married next summer.
tip: French marries reflexively: se marier, literally 'to marry oneself'. Ils se marieront = they'll get married. Without se, marier means to marry someone else off.

target: Les résultats seront publiés vendredi.
english: The results will be published on Friday.
tip: No word for 'on' with days: seront publiés vendredi = will be published on Friday. Add le – le vendredi – and it flips to mean every Friday.

target: Lorsque tu seras rentré, préviens-moi.
english: When you've gotten home, let me know.
tip: Futur antérieur with être: seras rentré. Rentrer uses être.

target: L'été prochain, nous visiterons la Bretagne.
english: Next summer, we'll visit Brittany.
tip: Visiter is for places, not people: nous visiterons la Bretagne. To visit a person you say rendre visite à, never visiter quelqu'un.

target: Elle aura trente ans en décembre.
english: She will be thirty in December.
tip: Age is something you have in French: elle aura trente ans = literally 'she will have thirty years'. Using être here is a classic English-speaker slip.

target: Nous finirons les travaux avant l'hiver.
english: We'll finish the work before winter.
tip: Travail becomes travaux in the plural, and les travaux specifically means construction or renovation work: finir les travaux = finish the building work.

target: Dès qu'elle sera prête, nous partirons.
english: As soon as she's ready, we'll leave.
tip: After dès que, French uses the future where English keeps the present: elle sera prête = literally 'she will be ready'. Both clauses go future.

target: J'aurais voulu être là pour t'aider.
english: I would have liked to be there to help you.
tip: Aurais voulu expresses regret about the past: j'aurais voulu être là = I would have liked to be there, meaning I wish I had been but wasn't.

target: Nous prendrons une décision après la réunion.
english: We'll make a decision after the meeting.
tip: You take a decision in French, not make one: nous prendrons une décision = we'll make a decision. Using faire here would sound wrong.

target: Je ne te décevrai pas, c'est promis.
english: I won't let you down, I promise.
tip: Décevoir means to disappoint, not to deceive – a false friend. Je ne te décevrai pas = I won't let you down. To deceive someone is tromper.

target: On va s'arrêter pour prendre de l'essence.
english: We're going to stop to get gas.
tip: Essence looks like the English 'essence' but means gasoline: on va prendre de l'essence = we'll get fuel. Perfume is un parfum, not essence.

target: Tu nous manqueras beaucoup quand tu partiras.
english: We'll miss you a lot when you leave.
tip: Manquer reverses things: tu nous manqueras = literally 'you will be missing to us'. The person missed is the subject, so tu me manques means 'I miss you'.

target: J'avais déjà vu ce film trois fois.
english: I had already seen this movie three times.
tip: In plus-que-parfait, adverbs like "déjà" go between the auxiliary and participle: avais déjà vu.

target: Les étudiants qui ont réussi l'examen sont contents.
english: The students who passed the exam are happy.
tip: Réussir l'examen means to pass the exam, not merely to succeed: qui ont réussi l'examen = who passed it. To fail it is rater or échouer à.

target: Je vais demander une augmentation à mon patron.
english: I'm going to ask my boss for a raise.
tip: Demander means to ask for, not to demand: demander une augmentation = to ask for a raise. And you ask it à someone – demander à mon patron.
